trickyParts: The fence is threaded explicitly from each queue's run() down to the eight continuations rather than kept as one shared counter, because subscribe, watchAgentStream and setEnvoyRole are also called outside any queue (envoy_subscribe, a resubscribe timer, the Legion claim bridge). A shared counter would fence those unqueued calls whenever an unrelated pass stalled, so envoy_subscribe would silently subscribe nothing during a stall.

setEnvoyRole throws AbandonedTaskError instead of returning false when its claim lands after its move was abandoned: false there means 'the listener refused the claim', which makes reassertRoleNow and settleRole end the role and record a refusal. settleRole catches it beside SessionLeftError, both meaning 'this move decided nothing'.

A pass abandoned at its deadline sets registrationFailed, the same flag a failed registration sets, so the next healthy tick re-asserts the role and fires the regain hook with reason 'reregistered'. That matters because the listener reaps a role claim whose holder left the session registry after one record lifetime, so a pane that stalled that long may be registered again and still not hold its role.
The queue swallows an abandoned task's eventual settlement. Oh My Pi treats an unhandled rejection as fatal (postmortem exitAfterFatal), so a wedged task that finally rejects must not surface.
deviations: The plan's design section 1 says the heartbeat's own re-registration fires when the last accepted registration is 'older than two refresh intervals'. It is implemented at one refresh interval. registeredAt is stamped when the listener's answer resolves - the posting tick plus the pass's work and the round trip - while ticks fire exactly one interval apart, so the tick at two intervals always measures an age just under two and skips, and the first self-refresh would be posted at the third interval: 300 s at the defaults, exactly the listener's 300 s record lifetime, i.e. the backstop would land at the instant the record expires. The ce-simplify-code efficiency reviewer found this; at one interval the live stall run posted the self-refresh 192 s after the last accepted registration, 108 s inside the lifetime. A healthy tick never reaches the branch (the healing latch is false), and the tick immediately after an accepted registration still skips, so no registration is duplicated.

Plan task 6 implied a new accessor for the resolved record lifetime. SessionRegistry already exports TTL() with the same semantics and five callers, one of them three statements from the new boot log line, so the boot log uses it and no accessor was added. (A RecordTTL duplicate was written first and removed by the simplify pass.)

The plan says the stall follows 'the shape the existing registry-outage warning already uses (envoy.ts:1648-1654): one context.ui.notify and one logger.warn'. That site has only a notify; the stall path emits both, behind its own once-per-episode flag beside the outage one, so the two never share a flag and a stall never also produces the plain 'registry heartbeat failed' notification.

The plan's acceptance-1 live proof wedges the third registration post 'at the change's head' with 'the plugin at the pull request's base commit' as the control. The control was run against c88a3a194c79, the merge-base on main, rather than the branch's planner commit 87098b9946bd; the two carry the same packages/pi-envoy/extensions/envoy.ts, and 87098b9946bd was used for the unit suite's negative control.
discoveredComplexity: context.ui.notify emits no frame on stdout in `omp --mode rpc --no-ui`, and logger.warn reaches no file a worker pod can find, so 'the pane or its log says that it happened' cannot be observed from outside the process. The live smoke's fixture registers a logger.registerLogSink and appends every warn entry to its observation log; that is how the one-stall-line assertion is made live.

The stall control has to run the base revision's plugin from inside packages/pi-envoy/extensions/, since the plugin imports ../src/... and ./envoy-message-renderer. The smoke materialises it as a dot-prefixed file there and removes it in its trap; a .gitignore entry covers a run that is killed before the trap runs.

An extension listed before the plugin with -e has its module body run first, which is what lets the fixture replace globalThis.fetch before createEnvoyClient captures it. Verified before the smoke was written.

packages/claude-envoy/dist/*.js embed the envoy-client constants and are checked by `bun run --cwd packages/claude-envoy check-dist`, so every change to envoy-settings.ts - the simplify pass's included - needs a rebuild.
